headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no shared I/O surfaces or write paths are documented, but marker can process documents while awesome-python is a non-runnable collection.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented: agent_a has no io_surfaces and network_egress is none, while agent_b also has no io_surfaces and use_mcp is false. With no bridge for agent_a outputs to reach agent_b as instructions, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, injection risk becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Do not add an MCP bridge without provenance tagging.
Review any future parser that treats file text as instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress:none, and agent_b cannot read_filesystem or write_filesystem. agent_a also has no documented data_classes_touched. With no shared workspace or outbound path, there is no documented leakage route between the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent gains network egress, outputs may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled for both agents.
Avoid mounting sensitive directories into either runtime.
Recheck permissions before enabling any file access.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a exposes no write or execution surface in the profile, and agent_b explicitly cannot write_filesystem, modify_git_state, execute_shell, or spawn_subprocesses. Since neither agent can mutate a shared resource, there is no documented capability overlap that can conflict.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given write or git capabilities, shared-resource conflicts could emerge.
IF agent_b is granted filesystem write or git mutation, coordination controls become necessary.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled for both agents.
Do not co-locate them on a mutable git checkout.
Add locking before any future shared-state writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a document-processing tool, so it may consume outputs from agent_a if orchestrated that way, but agent_a is only a collection repo and not runnable. The pair lacks documented action-taking authority, so any cascade is limited to misformatted or misleading documents rather than downstream operations.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds agent_a-generated text directly into agent_b without review, errors can propagate.
IF agent_b is used to produce final documents from agent_a outputs, verification gaps matter.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between the agents.
Require schema validation on agent_a outputs before agent_b consumes them.
Use a checklist to verify citations and facts.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either agent. Both profiles are open-source and touch no data_classes_touched, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies are introduced, they must be compared before deployment.
mitigations: Document the data classes before use.
Confirm residency and retention settings if sensitive data is introduced.
Avoid routing regulated data through either agent until reviewed.
